steps.body: The column algorithm is the area model written compactly: each place of the top number is multiplied by the single digit, and the pieces stack up.
steps.narration: The column algorithm is the area model written compactly: each place of the top number is multiplied by the single digit, and the pieces stack up.

widget.prompt: Work 1,342 × 3 in columns. Tap each column to multiply it.

commonResults.feedback: 3,026 stranded the carry out of the hundreds — a column keeps one digit and hands the rest upward.
One carry never joined the column above it, so the product is a whole hundred short.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Add column by column from the ones; when a column reaches 10 or more, trade and carry.
widget.successFeedback: 24,681 + 13,247 = 37,928 — the ones make 8 with a carry that the tens must include.

predict.prompt: Multiplying 1,342 × 3, how many columns get multiplied?
predict.reveal: Every place of 1,342 is part of the number, so every place is multiplied by 3.

cml.actionGoal: Split a factor into places, build each piece, and reassemble the whole for g4m 4x1.
invariants: Splitting a factor never changes the product: every piece of the split multiplies the other factor, and the pieces add back to exactly the same total, which is what makes g4m 4x1 decomposable at all.
misconceptions: Adding only some of the partial products, dropping or inventing a zero when factors carry tens, or letting a remainder reach or exceed the divisor.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one partial product were left out, exactly how much of the total would go missing?

widget.prompt: Use an area model for 32 × 5. What is the product?

commonErrors.feedback: That is only the tens piece (30 × 5). The ones piece 2 × 5 still has to be added on.
That is only the ones piece. The 30 in 32 contributes 30 × 5 as well.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Split a factor into its places, multiply each part, and add every piece back.
